stem: A 24-year-old man with schizophrenia on an antipsychotic is seen drinking from the ward tap many times a day, about 6 L daily, and says he is not especially thirsty. Serum sodium is 120 mEq/L and urine osmolality is 80 mOsm/kg. He is then kept from fluids under supervision for several hours, followed by an injection of desmopressin.
oneliner: 24M + schizophrenia + drinking ~6 L/day + Na 120 + urine osm 80 + supervised water deprivation then desmopressin → plasma osm, urine osm, response?
ask: Which set of baseline plasma osmolality, urine osmolality after water deprivation and response to desmopressin is expected?

options.A: Plasma osmolality ↑; urine stays dilute after deprivation, concentrates after desmopressin
options.B: Plasma osmolality ↑; urine stays dilute after deprivation and after desmopressin
options.C: Plasma osmolality ↓; urine already concentrated before any deprivation
options.D: Plasma osmolality ↓; urine concentrates after deprivation, little further rise with desmopressin
options.E: Plasma osmolality normal; urine concentrates partly after deprivation, further after desmopressin

whyNot.A: This is **central diabetes insipidus**; the patient's sodium is **low**, so plasma osmolality is low, not high
whyNot.B: This is **nephrogenic diabetes insipidus**, where plasma osmolality is **high**; his sodium of 120 makes it low
whyNot.C: Concentrated urine with low plasma osmolality is **SIADH**; his urine is **maximally dilute** (80)
whyNot.E: A further rise after desmopressin marks **partial central DI**; his sodium is **120**, so plasma osmolality is low

answer: Low plasma osmolality; urine concentrates with deprivation; no extra response to desmopressin
why: He is drinking so much that plasma osmolality and sodium fall, **ADH is suppressed** and urine is dilute. When water is withheld, plasma osmolality climbs, **ADH is released** and the kidney concentrates urine normally, so desmopressin adds **little**. In DI, urine would stay dilute despite rising plasma osmolality.
chain: Dilute urine of 80 mOsm/kg and low sodium
Water deprivation lets plasma osmolality rise
ADH returns and urine concentrates; desmopressin adds little

idea.rule: Primary polydipsia: low plasma osmolality at baseline, but the ADH axis and kidney respond normally once water is restricted.
also: Central DI: high plasma osmolality; dilute urine corrected by desmopressin
Nephrogenic DI: high plasma osmolality; dilute urine not corrected by desmopressin
SIADH: low plasma osmolality with inappropriately concentrated urine
Beer potomania and tea-and-toast diets: low sodium from excess free water
